named_mechanism: GlaMBIE consensus combination of multi-method glacier mass change estimates
definition: Systematic combination of regional glacier mass change estimates from multiple observational methods (glaciological, DEM differencing, altimetry, gravimetry) into a single consensus time series per region, then aggregated to global scale
assumptions: Annual variability can be transferred between data groups when one group lacks annual resolution
Glacier area changes are well-characterized and can be applied uniformly within regions
The 19 GTN-G regions provide an appropriate spatial decomposition
invariants: All 19 regions must be represented in the global total
Uncertainty must be propagated from individual estimates through to the consensus
Both Gt (total) and m w.e. (specific) representations must be consistent via glacier area
structural_steps: 1. Collect and homogenize input datasets to common temporal grid
2. Group by observational method (altimetry, gravimetry, DEM diff.+glaciological)
3. Combine within-group estimates into group-level solutions
4. Combine group-level solutions into regional consensus estimates
5. Convert hydrological year results to calendar year for global aggregation
6. Sum regional calendar year estimates for global total

fidelity_check.reason: We analyze the official GlaMBIE consensus results rather than re-implementing the combination algorithm, as the combination was performed by the GlaMBIE team with full access to all methodological details
fidelity_check.deviation_from_named_method: None - we use the published GlaMBIE results directly
